issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines an Animal constructor with two parameters (Animal(String, int)), but the solution's Animal class only provides a single-parameter constructor Animal(String). This constructor-parameter mismatch will confuse students about the required constructor signature and prevents them from following the UML that demands an age field initialized via the two-argument constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal constructor match the UML: add a constructor Animal(String name, int age) that initializes both fields. Update all subclasses' constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) to accept and pass the age to super(name, age). Alternatively, if age is intentionally omitted, update the problem statement/UML to remove the age attribute and the two-parameter constructor to avoid mismatch.

issues.description: The UML and problem statement show Animal has two attributes (name: String and age: int), but the solution's Animal class only defines the name attribute and omits age. This attribute mismatch contradicts the UML and the textual requirement that constructors should initialize all class attributes.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the missing age attribute to Animal (private int age), provide corresponding getter and setter, and ensure constructors initialize it. Also update subclasses and any code that constructs Animal instances to provide the age. Alternatively, revise the UML/problem statement to remove age if it was not intended.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares Animal with two attributes (name and age) and a constructor Animal(String, int), but both the template example code and the solution use a single-argument constructor (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle")) and an Animal implementation with only a name attribute and constructor Animal(String). This mismatch in the expected constructor signature/attributes creates confusion for students about how to implement Animal and its subclasses (should they include an age field and a two-argument constructor or not?).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Animal constructor/attributes consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement (UML and text) to specify only a name and a single-argument constructor Animal(String), or (B) update the template and solution to add an 'age' field and a two-argument constructor Animal(String, int), and adjust all subclass constructors and example usages (e.g., Seal, Pig, Goat and Main) to pass the age to super. Prefer updating the problem statement to match the simpler single-argument design if age is not required by the exercises.
